correctness.rationale: The stated graph is exactly a twisted two-rail ladder, not the ordinary prism. For n>=4 its n canonical squares are all four-cycles. Every perfect matching with a rung has uniquely forced even horizontal runs and thus a unique matching S of the n-cycle; no-rung cases are two boundary matchings, represented when n is even and frozen extras when n is odd. A switch changes S by exactly one cycle edge. Direct enumeration and a separate independent-set construction both executed for n=4..16, with expected matchings/components, nF_(n-1) edges and diameter 2floor(n/2). The unlimited-n conclusion follows from the explicit bijection and distance proof; experimental bounds are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The specified result is the isomorphism between the perfect-matching four-cycle-switch graph of every Möbius ladder and the Lucas cube, including complete parity-sensitive frozen-sector and exact metric characterization. The Lucas graph, its counts, and two unusual odd-width perfect matchings are expressly credited. Primary full-text comparisons distinguish a switch graph (a graph of perfect-matching configurations) from Lucas-cube structure in independent-set Hasse diagrams and from the very different perfect-matching simplicial complex. No covering all-width four-cycle-switch isomorphism was found; unindexed prior treatment remains possible.

value.rationale: For a canonical infinite family of nonorientable cubic graphs, the natural local dimer reconfiguration space is classified completely as a classical Lucas cube with precisely identified additional frozen states in the odd case. This connects dimer flips to a well-studied isometric partial-cube configuration geometry and proves exact all-width switch distances, connectivity and edge counts. It is not a small arbitrary statistic or isolated numerical check; the newly established bijection is the structural result.
